proposals.before: Injustice against Yu enraged the capital.
proposals.after: The crown prince had been deposed through no fault of his own, and people were indignant and resentful.
proposals.reason: s0107 太子既廢非其罪，眾情憤怨 names deposition without crime and popular indignation. The before invents “the capital” and drops 非其罪.

proposals.before: "You serve the empress and are close to her. Everyone says you knew in advance of the prince’s deposition. If trouble breaks out, disaster will surely reach you too."
proposals.after: You serve the empress and are close to her. Everyone says you knew in advance of the prince’s deposition. If trouble breaks out, disaster will surely reach you too.
proposals.reason: s0109 continues the speech opened at s0108 「 and closed at s0110 」. The wrapping quotation marks on this middle unit falsely close the speech; removing only that pair preserves the boundary. The remaining English matches 奉事中宮，與賈后親密 and 皆云豫知.

proposals.before: Sun Xiu sold the plot to Sima Lun.
proposals.after: Sun Xiu relayed the plan to Lun, the Prince of Zhao, and Lun wholeheartedly accepted it.
proposals.reason: s0111 秀言于趙王倫，倫深納焉 is report and wholehearted acceptance. “Sold the plot” invents a sale.

proposals.before: Lun was branded Jia's man.
proposals.after: You have long served Empress Jia; everyone in the streets and lanes considers you a partisan of the Jia clan.
proposals.reason: s0113 is still Sun Xiu’s speech to 明公: 素事賈后 and 街談巷議，皆以公為賈氏之黨. The before shifts to third-person narration and drops the street talk.

proposals.before: Yu would not thank Lun for a late defection.
proposals.after: Even if you now seek to perform a great service for the crown prince, he may suppress his old resentment, but he will certainly not reward you. He will think that you changed sides only under pressure from the people's wishes, hoping to escape punishment.
proposals.reason: s0114 今雖欲建大功于太子…必不能加賞於公，當謂公逼百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳. The before compresses this into an unstated late defection.

proposals.before: One slip and Lun's head would roll.
proposals.after: If you give any grounds for blame, you still will not escape execution.
proposals.reason: s0115 若有瑕釁，猶不免誅 is execution if a flaw appears, still in second person. “Lun's head would roll” invents the image and names the wrong grammatical subject.

proposals.before: Sun Xiu spread rumors of a palace plot to restore Yu.
proposals.after: Sun Xiu then had disinformation circulated, claiming that men in the palace wished to depose Empress Jia and bring the crown prince back.
proposals.reason: s0118 秀因使反間，言殿中人欲廢賈后，迎太子 names palace men, deposing Jia, and welcoming the crown prince. The before keeps only a restore-Yu rumor.

proposals.before: Jia panicked and had Cheng Ju mix purgative poison.
proposals.after: When Empress Jia heard this, she became anxious and afraid. She ordered Cheng Ju, the chief court physician, to compound pills from croton and apricot kernels.
proposals.reason: s0119 賈后聞之憂怖，乃使太醫令程據合巴豆杏子丸. “Purgative poison” is not in the Chinese; 太醫令 and 巴豆杏子丸 are.

proposals.before: Third month a fake edict sent Sun Lü to kill Yu at Xuchang.
proposals.after: In the third month, she forged an edict and sent the Yellow Gate attendant Sun Lü to carry the pills to Xuchang and kill the crown prince.
proposals.reason: s0120 三月，矯詔使黃門孫慮齋至許昌以害太子 restores the third month, forged edict, 黃門, 齋至許昌, and harming the crown prince. 齋 continues the pills of s0119.

proposals.before: Yu had cooked for himself to avoid cup poison.
proposals.after: Earlier, fearing that he would be poisoned, the crown prince always cooked his own food in front of himself.
proposals.reason: s0121 恆自煮食於前 is that he himself cooked the food before him. The host after restores 恐見鴆 and 初 but weakens 自煮 into having food cooked for him.

proposals.before: Sun Lü beat Yu to death in the latrine with a pestle—screams escaped.
proposals.after: Sun Lü then tried to force the medicine on the crown prince, but he refused to take it. When the crown prince went to the privy, Lü beat him to death with a medicine pestle. The crown prince cried out loudly, and his cries could be heard outside.
proposals.reason: s0123 逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，因如廁，慮以藥杵椎殺之，太子大呼，聲聞於外. The before drops the refused medicine and the loud cry heard outside.

proposals.before: He died at twenty-three.
proposals.after: He was then twenty-three by traditional reckoning.
proposals.reason: s0124 時年二十三 is age at the time, not an added verb “died.” Traditional reckoning is preserved; no Western year is introduced.

proposals.before: Sima Yu, styled Xizu, was Emperor Hui's firstborn—his mother was Lady Xie of Talented rank.
proposals.after: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
proposals.reason: s0002 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人. The idiomatic line drops the Minhuai title and 長子.

proposals.before: Wu Di doted on the bright boy and kept him always near.
proposals.after: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
proposals.reason: s0003 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右.

proposals.before: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'
proposals.after: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'
proposals.reason: s0004 次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」 The 帝 who speaks is Emperor Wu, as the sealed literal already has; idiomatic “the emperor” can be read as Hui.

proposals.before: A night blaze drew Wu Di to a high gallery.
proposals.after: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.
proposals.reason: s0006 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之.

proposals.before: Five-year-old Yu pulled his grandfather into the dark.
proposals.after: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.
proposals.reason: s0007 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中 names 帝 and 裾, not “grandfather.”

proposals.before: While watching the imperial sty he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"
proposals.after: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"
proposals.reason: s0010 嘗從帝觀豕牢.

proposals.before: He likened the heir to Sima Yi before court—reputation followed.
proposals.after: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.
proposals.reason: s0013 嘗對群臣稱太子似宣帝，於是令譽流於天下. 宣帝 is the title in this unit; Sima Yi is not written here.

proposals.before: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
proposals.after: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.
proposals.reason: s0205 lists 太保, 太子太傅, 太子少師, 太子少傅, and 尚書令 with the fathers' names.

proposals.before: Adult Yu spurned books, slighted tutors, and played with pages.
proposals.after: When grown he cared nothing for study and only played games with attendants; he could not honor tutors or guardians.
proposals.reason: s0014 及長，不好學，惟與左右嬉戲，不能尊敬保傅. 左右 are attendants, not pages.

proposals.before: When Consort Jiang bore a son they pushed costly toys and stipends—Yu complied.
proposals.after: When Lady Jiang, whom the crown prince favored, bore a son, they also said rewards should be lavish and many toys fashioned for the imperial grandson; the crown prince obeyed.
proposals.reason: s0017 太子所幸蔣美人生男，又言宜隆其賞賜，多為皇孫造玩弄之器，太子從之.

proposals.before: He skipped audiences for back-garden games.
proposals.after: Thereupon his arrogance and laxness grew plainer; sometimes he skipped court attendance and constantly played in the rear garden.
proposals.reason: s0018 於是慢弛益彰，或廢朝侍，恆在後園遊戲.

proposals.before: He thrashed servants himself.
proposals.after: If anyone offended him he personally beat them.
proposals.reason: s0020 或有犯忤者，手自捶擊之.

proposals.before: He banned builders from touching plaster or tiles—superstition.
proposals.after: Given to petty taboos, he forbade plastering walls, repairing fences, or straightening roof-tiles.
proposals.reason: s0021 性拘小忌，不許繕壁修牆，正瓦動屋. “Superstition” is not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: He peddled greens, dye seed, chicken, and flour from West Garden for cash.
proposals.after: He also ordered the Western Garden to sell mallow, indigo seed, chickens, flour, and the like, pocketing the profit.
proposals.reason: s0024 又令西園賣葵菜、藍子、雞、面之屬，而收其利.

proposals.before: Jiang Tong's five memorials went unheard—see his chapter.
proposals.after: Groom of the Household Jiang Tong presented five admonitions; the crown prince rejected them—the account appears in Jiang Tong's biography.
proposals.reason: s0026 洗馬江統陳五事以諫之，太子不納，語在《統傳》中.

proposals.before: Yu refused to flatter Jia Mi.
proposals.after: The crown prince's temper was stiff; knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.
proposals.reason: s0029 太子性剛，知賈謐恃後之貴，不能假借之.

proposals.before: He left Jia Mi cooling heels while he played inside.
proposals.after: When Mi came to the Eastern Palace he sometimes left him waiting while he played in the inner courts.
proposals.reason: s0030 謐至東宮，或舍之而於後庭遊戲.

proposals.before: Yu resented losing Wang's elder beauty to Jia Mi.
proposals.after: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.
proposals.reason: s0036 太子聞衍長女美，而賈后為謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言.

proposals.before: Jia adopted the plot and smeared Yu empire-wide.
proposals.after: The empress accepted his words and further broadcast the crown prince's faults throughout near and far.
proposals.reason: s0041 後納其言，又宣揚太子之短，布諸遠近.

proposals.before: Zhao Jun urged preemptive deposition—Yu declined.
proposals.after: Central Guard Zhao Jun asked the crown prince to depose the empress first; the crown prince refused.
proposals.reason: s0043 中護軍趙俊請太子廢後，太子不聽.

proposals.before: Twelfth month Jia feigned imperial illness to lure Yu to court.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month, when Empress Jia would depose the crown prince, she falsely claimed the emperor was unwell and summoned the crown prince to court.
proposals.reason: s0045 十二月，賈后將廢太子，詐稱上不和，呼太子入朝.

proposals.before: She hid him, fed him wine and dates through Chen Wu until he was drunk.
proposals.after: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.
proposals.reason: s0046 既至，後不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞賜以酒棗，逼飲醉之.

proposals.before: Or I will finish you.
proposals.after: if you do not end it yourself, I shall come in and end it for you.
proposals.reason: s0049 不自了，吾當入了之 continues the forged text of s0048.

proposals.before: Consort Xie and I strike together—no delay.
proposals.after: Together with Consort Xie we agreed a joint date for simultaneous rising—do not hesitate and breed later trouble.
proposals.reason: s0052 並謝妃共要克期而兩發，勿疑猶豫，致後患.

proposals.before: Then sacrifice to the Northern Lord and amnesty all.
proposals.after: When the wish is fulfilled we shall sacrifice three victims to the Northern Lord and proclaim an empire-wide amnesty.
proposals.reason: s0054 願成，當三牲祠北君，大赦天下.

proposals.before: So commands the spell.'
proposals.after: Let this sworn petition take effect as commanded."
proposals.reason: s0055 要疏如律令. “Spell” is not in the Chinese; this closes the forged text opened at s0048.

proposals.before: Helpers patched characters before Jia showed Hui.
proposals.after: They afterward filled them in; the empress presented it to the emperor.
proposals.reason: s0057 既而補成之，后以呈帝.

proposals.before: Silence fell until Zhang Hua and Pei Wei defended Yu.
proposals.after: It was shown all around to the lords and princes; none spoke, except Zhang Hua and Pei Wei, who verified the crown prince's innocence.
proposals.reason: s0059 遍示諸公王，莫有言者，惟張華、裴頠證明太子.

proposals.before: Debate stalled till dusk.
proposals.after: Deliberation lasted until sunset unresolved.
proposals.reason: s0061 議至日西不決.

proposals.before: Jia feared delay—demoted Yu to commoner instead.
proposals.after: The empress feared events might shift and therefore memorialized to degrade the crown prince to commoner status; an edict approved.
proposals.reason: s0062 後懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之.

proposals.before: Next New Year Jia staged a Yellow Gate confession implicating Yu.
proposals.after: The next first month Empress Jia again had a Yellow Gate confess plotting rebellion with the crown prince.
proposals.reason: s0066 明年正月，賈后又使黃門自首，欲與太子為逆. “New Year” and “staged” are not the Chinese.

proposals.before: Wang Yan filed for divorce the moment Yu fell.
proposals.after: When the crown prince was first deposed, his father-in-law Wang Yan memorialized requesting divorce.
proposals.reason: s0073 初，太子之廢也，妃父王衍表請離婚.

proposals.before: He claimed dutiful service to Jia despite birth.
proposals.after: Though not born of the inner palace I served her as my own mother.
proposals.reason: s0075 continues the letter: 雖非中宮所生，奉事有如親母.

proposals.before: Palace rules barred him from Lady Xie.
proposals.after: Since becoming crown prince, edicts confined me—I could not see my mother.
proposals.reason: s0076 自為太子以來，敕見禁檢，不得見母. Lady Xie is not named in this unit.

proposals.before: His plea for son's title failed.
proposals.after: Then I petitioned the throne for honors—permission never came.
proposals.reason: s0079 于時表國家乞加徽號，不見聽許.

proposals.before: He denied malice in praying for the boy.
proposals.after: When the illness grew grave I sought blessings for him—I bore no evil intent.
proposals.reason: s0080 疾病既篤，為之求請恩福，無有噁心.

proposals.before: He requested audience.
proposals.after: At once I drafted a memorial begging entry.
proposals.reason: s0083 即便作表求入.

proposals.before: He saw Hui briefly then reached Jia's halls.
proposals.after: On the twenty-ninth morning I entered and saw His Majesty; presently I was sent to the inner palace.
proposals.reason: s0084 二十九日早入見國家，須臾遣至中宮.

proposals.before: Chen Wu claimed Jia was sick.
proposals.after: Inner attendants Chen Wu told me: 'The empress vomited ill this morning.'
proposals.reason: s0085 中宮左右陳舞見語：'中宮旦來吐不快。'

proposals.before: They parked him in an empty room.
proposals.after: She told me to wait seated in an empty chamber.
proposals.reason: s0086 使住空屋中坐.

proposals.before: Chen Wu forced three sheng wine and dates.
proposals.after: She brought three sheng of ale and a great tray of jujubes and made him finish both.
proposals.reason: s0089 便持三升酒、大盤棗來見與，使飲酒啖棗盡.

proposals.before: Yu pleaded low tolerance.
proposals.after: I never drink ale, yet sent Chen Wu back explaining I could not manage three sheng.
proposals.reason: s0090 鄙素不飲酒，即便遣舞啟說不堪三升之意.

proposals.before: Yu cited earlier imperial banquet.
proposals.after: I answered the inner palace: His Majesty granted ale one day—therefore I dared not refuse—but all day I never drank three sheng.
proposals.reason: s0093 便答中宮：'陛下會同一日見賜，故不敢辭，通日不飲三升酒也。'

proposals.before: Empty stomach worried him.
proposals.after: Moreover I had not eaten—I feared I could not endure it.
proposals.reason: s0094 且實未食，恐不堪.

proposals.before: Chen Wu called him unfilial.
proposals.after: Chen Wu relayed another message: "You unfilial wretch!
proposals.reason: s0096 陳舞復傳語云：'不孝那！' continues into s0097.

proposals.before: Cornered he drank more.
proposals.after: Pressed helplessly he drank another sheng.
proposals.reason: s0099 逼迫不得已，更飲一升.

proposals.before: He found white and green paper inside.
proposals.after: I started in alarm and looked: there was one sheet of white paper and one of green.
proposals.reason: s0102 鄙便驚起，視之，有一白紙，一青紙.

proposals.before: Runners said the emperor waited.
proposals.after: They pressed: 'His Majesty is waiting.'
proposals.reason: s0103 催促云：'陛下停待。'

proposals.before: Chengfu added brush and yellow paper for the copy.
proposals.after: Another small maid, Chengfu, brought brush, inkstone, and yellow paper, making him write.
proposals.reason: s0104 又小婢承福持筆研墨黃紙來，使寫.

proposals.before: Rush left no time to read the forgery's sense.
proposals.after: Haste would not let me reread; I truly did not notice the import of the words on the page.
proposals.reason: s0105 急疾不容復視，實不覺紙上語輕重. “Forgery” is not in this unit.

proposals.before: She claimed thwarted maternal hopes.
proposals.after: That aim failed—doubly bitter regret.
proposals.reason: s0127 此志不遂，重以酸恨 continues Jia's memorial.

proposals.before: She asked royal burial despite his crimes.
proposals.after: Though Yu's guilt was utmost he remains an imperial grandson—to dispatch him as a mere commoner is truly pitiable—may Heaven grant kingly burial.
proposals.reason: s0128 遹雖罪在莫大，猶王者子孫，便以匹庶送終，情實憐湣，特乞天恩，賜以王禮.

proposals.before: The court buried him as Guangling prince.
proposals.after: An edict buried him with rites due the Prince of Guangling.
proposals.reason: s0130 詔以廣陵王禮葬之.

proposals.before: Court mourned and fetched Yu's bier from Xu.
proposals.after: The emperor wore unhemmed mourning for the crown prince as for an eldest son; the ministers wore hemmed mourning. He sent Minister He Yu to lead the Eastern Palace officials in preparing the prescribed auspicious and mourning rites and bringing the crown prince's bier back from Xuchang.
proposals.reason: s0141 帝為太子服長子斬衰，群臣齊衰，使尚書和郁率東宮官屬具吉凶之制，迎太子喪于許昌.

proposals.before: Storm shattered funeral umbrellas.
proposals.after: When the hearse set out, great wind and thunder came—canopies and coverings flew torn.
proposals.reason: s0142 喪之發也，大風雷電，幃蓋飛裂.

proposals.before: Courtiers weep together.
proposals.after: Shared grief and equal pain—who lacks bitter sorrow!
proposals.reason: s0165 同悲等痛，孰不酸辛.

proposals.before: Buried sixth month at Xianping.
proposals.after: On jimao day of the sixth month he was buried at Xianping Mausoleum.
proposals.reason: s0168 六月己卯，葬于顯平陵.

proposals.before: Yan Zuan's plea built Son-Lament Terrace—Jiang Tong and Lu Ji wrote elegies.
proposals.after: Moved by Yan Zuan's words the emperor raised a Terrace of Longing for Sons; former ministers Jiang Tong and Lu Ji both composed dirges.
proposals.reason: s0169 帝感閻纘之言，立思子台，故臣江統、陸機並作誄頌焉.

proposals.before: Three sons shared Yu's prison.
proposals.after: The crown prince had three sons—Bin, Zang, and Shang—all imprisoned with their father at Jinyong.
proposals.reason: s0170 太子三子：虨、臧、尚，並與父同幽金墉.

proposals.before: Eldest Bin (Daowen) died Yongkang first month.
proposals.after: Bin, courtesy name Daowen, died in the first month of Yongkang year one.
proposals.reason: s0171 虨字道文，永康元年正月，薨.

proposals.before: Fourth month titled Prince of Nanyang.
proposals.after: In the fourth month he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang.
proposals.reason: s0172 四月，追封南陽王.

proposals.before: Yongkang fourth month made Linhuai prince.
proposals.after: In the fourth month of Yongkang year one he was enfeoffed Prince of Linhuai.
proposals.reason: s0174 永康元年四月，封臨淮王.

proposals.before: Zang named grand-heir.
proposals.after: Now we establish Zang as imperial grandson-heir.
proposals.reason: s0176 今立臧為皇太孫.

proposals.before: Staff slid from heir to grand-heir titles.
proposals.after: Eastern Palace staff transferred to grand-heir posts.
proposals.reason: s0178 太子官屬即轉為太孫官屬.

proposals.before: May procession exited the west palace gate in Yu's old livery.
proposals.after: In the fifth month Lun and the grand heir went together to the Eastern Palace; the grand heir exited the Western Side Gate—carriages, dress, and attendants all followed Minhuai's old train.
proposals.reason: s0180 五月，倫與太孫俱之東宮，太孫自西掖門出，車服侍從皆湣懷之舊也.

proposals.before: Luoyang wept along Bronze Camel Street.
proposals.after: Reaching Bronze Camel Avenue palace women wept; attendants choked; passersby wiped tears.
proposals.reason: s0181 到銅駝街，宮人哭，侍從者皆哽咽，路人抆淚焉.

proposals.before: Omen mulberry mirrored heir's fall.
proposals.after: The mulberry sprouted again west of the wing; when the grand heir was deposed it withered.
proposals.reason: s0182 桑復生於西廂，太孫廢，乃枯.

proposals.before: Yongning coup demoted Zang—murdered at Jinyong.
proposals.after: In the first month of Yongning year one Lun, Prince of Zhao, usurped the throne and demoted Zang to Prince of Puyang. Zang moved with the emperor to Jinyong and was murdered soon afterward.
proposals.reason: s0183 永甯元年正月，趙王倫篡位，廢為濮陽王，與帝俱遷金墉，尋被害.

proposals.before: Tai'an era canonized Ai.
proposals.after: Early in Tai'an the posthumous title Ai was granted.
proposals.reason: s0184 太安初，追諡曰哀.

proposals.before: Wu Di planned Yu as future pillar.
proposals.after: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.
proposals.reason: s0186 武皇鍾愛，既深詒厥之謀.

proposals.before: The realm expected greatness.
proposals.after: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.
proposals.reason: s0187 天下歸心，頗有後來之望.

proposals.before: Posthumous honors could not resurrect him.
proposals.after: Though mourning rites ran full and grief ran deep, what did they mend for the poisoned innocent!

additionalRepairs.before: She told you to wait seated in an empty chamber.
additionalRepairs.after: She told me to wait seated in an empty chamber.
additionalRepairs.reason: 使住空屋中坐 continues the first-person letter; “you” is the wrong person.

additionalRepairs.before: She brought three sheng of ale and a great tray of jujubes and made him finish both.
additionalRepairs.after: She brought three sheng of ale and a great tray of jujubes and made me finish both.
additionalRepairs.reason: The letter is first person; 使飲酒啖棗盡 is what was done to the writer.

additionalRepairs.reason: 逼迫不得已，更飲一升 continues the first-person letter.
